source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New York's only data center with a published power figure is a 3 MW CyrusOne colocation campus, far smaller than the 50 to 100 MW a single modern GPU cluster can draw.

The state has 31 mapped data center locations. Exactly one of them publishes an IT capacity number. That gap is the real finding: New York's data center map is mostly a map of addresses, not of electrical load. The one facility that does disclose, CyrusOne's NYM7 in Wappingers Falls, holds 100,000 square feet of technical space and 3 MW of IT capacity, which at a conservative 30 kW per rack works out to roughly 100 racks.

For AI specifically, this is a compliance asset rather than a compute asset. SSAE 16 Type II certification qualifies the site for workloads that need audited financial and operational controls. At 3 MW it cannot host a large training run or inference cluster as a standalone facility. Nothing in the data indicates this campus is an AI site, and its status as the state's only published figure reflects how little operators disclose, not dominance within the state's portfolio.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. The capacity of the other 30 New York locations is unknown, so no total for the state's AI-relevant compute can be derived. There is no announced expansion, no grid or power supply detail, and no address. The 46 suitability score is built only from published IT capacity and operator type, which makes it a measure of disclosure as much as of infrastructure.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
